newsitem.title: INDIA: Floods claim 12 lives in India's northeast region.
newsitem.headline: Floods claim 12 lives in India's northeast region.

text.p: Flash floods and landslides killed at least 12 people and left many homeless in India's northeastern region, officials said on Thursday.
Seven districts of the Arunachal Pradesh and five districts in Assam were affected by the floods which followed non-stop rains in the last few days, they said.
Officials said the state capital Itanagar of Arunachal Pradesh was cut off from other parts of the country by landslides. Transport and telecommunication networks in the region have been paralysed.
Authorities in the affected states have asked the army to assist in rescue operations.
Weather forecasters have forecast more rains in the region in the coming days.
However, work in the region's more than 800 tea gardens and oil-drilling sites has not been affected, officials said.
The region, consisting of seven hill states is surrounded by Bhutan, Bangladesh, Burma and China and is home to more than 200 ethnic groups.
All rivers in the region including the main river Brahmaputra are flowing above the danger mark, the officials said.
